speed = 2

print(hours)
# The whole hours, with the decimal part cut off

cards.why: int() cuts off everything after the decimal point; it does not round up. So int(7.9) is 7, even though 7.9 is close to 8.

class Hero:

        self.name = name
        self.health = 10

    def take_hit(self, damage):
        self.health = max(0, self.health - damage)

    def is_alive(self):
        return self.health > 0

nova = Hero("Nova")
kai = Hero("Kai")
nova.take_hit(4)
kai.take_hit(15)
print(nova.health, nova.is_alive())
print(kai.health, kai.is_alive())
cards.why: Nova and Kai are separate objects with their own health. Hitting Nova changes nothing about Kai.

cards.prompt: This should print 12, but prints 5. Which line has the bug?
cards.code:
for n in [3, 4, 5]:
    total = 0
    total = total + n
print(total)
cards.fixed:
total = 0
for n in [3, 4, 5]:
    total = total + n
print(total)
cards.why: total = 0 inside the loop wipes the total every turn. It belongs above the loop.

cards.prompt: It should print every step from 1 to 5. Which line has the bug?
cards.why: range stops before its second number, so range(1, 5) ends at 4.

cards.prompt: This stops with a TypeError. Which line is the real cause?
cards.why: double() prints instead of returning, so it gives back None, and None + 1 fails on line 4.

cards.prompt: This stops with an UnboundLocalError. Which line is the cause?
cards.code:
score = 0

def win():
    score = score + 1

win()
cards.fixed:
score = 0

def win(score):
    return score + 1

score = win(score)
cards.why: Assigning to score inside win() makes it local, and the local one has no value yet when score + 1 runs.

cards.prompt: This should print refused, but stops with a TypeError. Which line has the bug?
cards.why: raise needs an error, such as ValueError("too young"), not plain text.

cards.prompt: This stops with an AttributeError. Which line is the real cause?

cards.prompt: A program reads one settings record when it starts, and never changes it. Which fits best?
cards.why: One record, no actions, no copies: a dictionary holds it with no extra code. A class would add a shape with nothing to do.

cards.prompt: Which belongs on the not-yet list for a first version of Lockpick?
cards.code:
# A brief, kept as Python data
brief = {
    "project": "Lockpick",
    "for": "my brother, who likes word games",
    "must": [
        "guess one letter at a time",
        "six misses and the lock jams",
        "play again",
    ],
    "not yet": ["hints", "two players"],
}
print(brief["project"], "for", brief["for"])
for feature in brief["must"]:
    print("-", feature)
print("Not yet:", ", ".join(brief["not yet"]))
options: A hint that costs a try
Showing the word as _ a _ _ t
cards.why: The other two are what make it Lockpick at all. A hint is an extra: good to have, but the game works without it.
